Week 3. Pattern: hash map lookup.

A reconciliation clerk knows two transfers (amounts in kobo) add up to target. Return the indices [i, j] with i < j of the first such pair found scanning left to right (smallest j), or an empty array if there is none. Aim for O(n) time.

Complete the class TwoSumTransfers in the answer box, keeping these signatures:

  • public static int[] find(long[] amounts, long target)

Use only the Java standard library. Click Check to run the tests; you can check as often as you like with no penalty. Say your approach and its time complexity out loud before you code.

generalfeedback.text: Pattern: hash map lookup. Compare your answer with the reference solution in practice/dsa/solutions, then write one line in your NOTES.md: the pattern, the complexity, and the mistake you made.

Week 4. Pattern: grouping with a map.

Given postings (account number and a signed amount in kobo: credits positive, debits negative), return each account's net total, ordered by total descending and, for equal totals, by account number ascending.

Complete the class TotalsByAccount in the answer box, keeping these signatures:

  • public record Posting(String account, long amountKobo)
  • public static LinkedHashMap<String, Long> totals(List<Posting> postings)

Use only the Java standard library. Click Check to run the tests; you can check as often as you like with no penalty. Say your approach and its time complexity out loud before you code.

generalfeedback.text: Pattern: grouping with a map. Compare your answer with the reference solution in practice/dsa/solutions, then write one line in your NOTES.md: the pattern, the complexity, and the mistake you made.

testcode.text: System.out.println(TotalsByAccount.totals(List.of( new TotalsByAccount.Posting("0003", 5_000), new TotalsByAccount.Posting("0001", 10_000), new TotalsByAccount.Posting("0002", 7_000), new TotalsByAccount.Posting("0001", -3_000), new TotalsByAccount.Posting("0003", 2_000), new TotalsByAccount.Posting("0004", -100))));

Week 9. Pattern: digit processing.

Return whether a card number passes the Luhn check. Spaces are allowed between digits; any other non-digit, or fewer than 13 or more than 19 digits, makes it invalid. Starting from the rightmost digit, double every second digit, subtract 9 from doubled values above 9, sum everything; valid if the sum is a multiple of 10.

Complete the class Luhn in the answer box, keeping these signatures:

  • public static boolean isValid(String pan)

Use only the Java standard library. Click Check to run the tests; you can check as often as you like with no penalty. Say your approach and its time complexity out loud before you code.

questiontext.text:
Week 9. Pattern: weighted checksum.

A 10-digit NUBAN account number is a 9-digit serial plus a check digit computed with the bank's 3-digit code (CBN NUBAN standard). Multiply the 12 digits of bankCode + serial by the weights 3,7,3,3,7,3,3,7,3,3,7,3, sum them, and the check digit is 10 - (sum % 10), with 10 becoming 0. Inputs that are not exactly 3 and 9 (or 10) digits throw IllegalArgumentException.

Complete the class NubanCheckDigit in the answer box, keeping these signatures:

  • public static int checkDigit(String bankCode, String serial)
  • public static boolean isValid(String bankCode, String accountNumber)

Use only the Java standard library. Click Check to run the tests; you can check as often as you like with no penalty. Say your approach and its time complexity out loud before you code.

Week 13. Pattern: sort then sweep.

Maintenance windows are given as [start, end] minutes (start ≤ end), in any order. Merge overlapping or touching windows ([1,3] and [3,5] become [1,5]) and return them sorted by start.

Complete the class MergeWindows in the answer box, keeping these signatures:

  • public record Window(int start, int end)
  • public static List<Window> merge(List<Window> windows)

Use only the Java standard library. Click Check to run the tests; you can check as often as you like with no penalty. Say your approach and its time complexity out loud before you code.
